plans.objective: [DIM: composition] The rigid family is defined by the linear PDE $f'(x) = 0$ (constant functions) with $w$ samples determining the single degree of freedom, while the fat family is defined by a normalized random polynomial basis of degree 19 with coefficients drawn from a standard normal distribution, ensuring O(1) scale and high-dimensional solution space. This directly addresses the run27 failure where dynamic range violated the zero-violation criterion, provides clear analytic ground truths, and maintains strict adherence to the ML/math problem domain without materials analogies.

steps.description: Implement the rigid and fat function families as specified in the hypothesis, ensuring proper normalization to O(1) scale, correct (N,1) shape for labels, non-overlapping held-out sets, and providing analytic ground truths. The rigid family uses constant functions (f'(x)=0) with w samples determining the single degree of freedom, while the fat family uses a normalized random polynomial basis of degree 19 with standard normal coefficients. This addresses the run27 failure by ensuring proper dynamic range and zero-violation criterion adherence.
